consequence.statement: Existing PolicyException objects stay stored as v2beta1 until rewritten; a storage version migration and a status.storedVersions update are needed before a later release removes v2beta1.
consequence.remediation: Re-write all PolicyException objects and update status.storedVersions before a later release removes v2beta1.

original.statement: The storage version of the policyexceptions.kyverno.io CRD changes from v2beta1 to v2, so existing objects stay stored as v2beta1 until a storage version migration is run and status.storedVersions is updated before v2beta1 is removed.

consequence.statement: After the upgrade, new and rewritten PolicyException objects are stored as v2. Existing objects stay stored as v2beta1 and keep working because v2beta1 is still served. Nothing fails in this release.
consequence.remediation: Before a later release removes v2beta1, rewrite all PolicyException objects so they are stored as v2, then remove v2beta1 from the CRD's status.storedVersions.

corrected.statement: In 1.13.0 the storage version of policyexceptions.kyverno.io moves from v2beta1 to v2, and v2beta1 is still served. Existing PolicyException objects keep working but stay stored as v2beta1 until they are rewritten. Review this and plan a storage migration before v2beta1 is removed.

decision.reason: [ev-094d5d8b0291] and [ev-f0f21b325fa6] show only that the storage flag moves from v2beta1 to v2 between 1.12.6 and 1.13.0. The CRD snapshots [ev-e4d8d307c8bd] and [ev-f5ab4321b780] show v2beta1 is still an API version in both releases, which the validator confirmed. Nothing in the evidence says that anything fails, is rejected or must be migrated before or after this upgrade. Existing objects keep working, and the migration only becomes necessary before some later, unscheduled release removes v2beta1, so migration-required (mandatory work) over-claims and this should be a review-class behavior-change.
